newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures retain firm tone in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures retain firm tone in late trade.

text.p: German Bund futures were expected to retain their firm bias on Wednesday after spending much of Tuesday afternoon trading in narrow, but higher ranges.
Bunds were helped by firm Treasury prices and the lack of any fundamental economic news that could have soured the market's mood with infationary worries.
The December DTB Bund future was up 12 basis points at 101.18 in late trade, but off a new contract high of 101.27 set in early trade.
Traders said that unless M3 money supply and Wednesday's Ifo report are stronger than expected, Bunds should firm.

Of the two, traders said the Ifo report is by far the most important. The Bundesbank is widely expected to keep rates on hold for the time being and is not likely to have its mind changed by the October M3 report.

Traders said assuming the two reports fail to ignite inflationary worries, Bunds should continue to climb. Some see the contract headed toward 101.36 -- what would be their highest level since January.
Bunds continued to trade roughly in line with U.S. debt as the spread remained stable around 46 basis points.
